mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market that pressures firms to raise wages and prices, compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for three consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two months, indicates a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 1% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decrease in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.25 percentage points indicates a coordinated easing of monetary and inflationary pressures, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both fall by >= 0.25% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 5% from the previous month, combined with a concurrent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving that foreshadows weaker earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 5% month-over-month and GDPC1 falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for four consecutive months signals a deepening labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) of at least 10% from the previous month for two consecutive months indicates a robust recovery in residential construction activity, which boosts materials and homebuilding equities and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises >= 10% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
